the extent of subjective information in a review is negatively associated with sales, but positively associated with perceived usefulness.
reviews that are more informative and more subjective are rated as more helpful, and reviews that are less informative and more objective are associated with higher product sales.

reviews that are written by users who are more experienced and have higher levels of expertise, are more likely to be rated as more useful by the readers, and are positively associated with product sales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extent of readability, subjectivity, and linguistic correctness of reviews are important factors in predicting the economic impact of reviews and their perceived usefulness.
the more informative and readable reviews are more helpful and positively impact sales.
reviews with more subjectivity are rated more informative by readers but are less effective in increasing product sales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are several factors, both in terms of text based as well as reviewer level features that influence the economic impact of a review and its perceived helpfulness.

the text based features are more important than the reviewer related features, and that the readability features are more important in estimating the economic impact of reviews, whereas the subjectivity features are more important for estimating perceived usefulness.
